title: Scoped scientific evidence report: iron-group nucleosynthesis
question: What do these two original papers establish about iron-group nucleosynthesis, and what remains unestablished about Earth's iron?

findings.statement: The authors identify explosion-mechanism uncertainty as a limitation on predictions for certain isotopic abundances.
The paper presents ejected isotope yields for modeled stars at different metallicities.
The authors calculate explosive nucleosynthesis for models varying deflagration speeds and ignition densities.
In the modeled Type Ia scenarios, the total amount of nickel-56 and the Si-Ca/Fe ratio depend on the deflagration-to-detonation transition density.
The modeled abundances of some neutron-rich iron-group isotopes are sensitive to electron capture.

comparison.method: The papers address distinct modeled explosion channels: massive-star explosions versus Chandrasekhar-mass Type Ia explosions.
comparison.results: Both discuss modeled nucleosynthesis and iron-group-related isotopes, but their yields have not been normalized or quantitatively compared by this laboratory.
comparison.limitations: Explosion physics and model parameters affect predicted isotope yields. These are source-specific statements, not a demonstrated cross-paper disagreement.

earth_iron.reason: Neither this limited two-paper comparison nor the extracted evidence quantifies the provenance of iron incorporated into the proto-solar nebula or Earth. Additional galactic chemical-evolution, solar-system formation, and isotopic evidence is required.

boundaries: The report does not independently verify semantic entailment or full-page context.
PDF pages refer to physical PDF pages, not necessarily printed journal pages.
The same excerpt repeated under several axes is one evidence item.
No inference is made about scriptural interpretation or a unique terrestrial iron source.
A green CI run validates traceability checks, not scientific truth.
